checks: Default description imports no numerical libraries and executes no data or device work.
Complete source-only evidence and root release precede loading; scientific endpoint fields are prohibited in the source-only contract.
Three batch pairs are chosen prospectively using count/source-order ranks 0/1, 500/501 and 998/999, with targets 6 and 150. Actual prospective batches are saved before CUDA configuration.
Original and candidate graphs share initial tensors, host noise and restored RNG. Ordered edges, ledgers and RNG invariance are checked before updates.
Two fresh updates per graph, arm and batch compare byte representations of network inputs, predictions, heads, targets, loss, gradients, tensors, Adam state and RNG.
Both small-case candidate arms replay step two from saved step-one checkpoint and compare serialized/restored and final payloads exactly.
Successful orchestration requires all six cases, twelve paired comparisons, both replays, 26 optimizer calls and nonzero optional-edge exposure.
Output is fresh and separate; interruption/numerical failure retains attempted-update information and best-effort unsuccessful state. Input and saved-batch hashes are reverified before success.

tests.scope: tiny synthetic CPU graph/update tests plus mocked CUDA orchestration, including failures before update zero and update four
tests.warnings: 105 existing torch.jit deprecation and frozen-source invalid-escape warnings; no test failures

limits: No actual training arrays, CUDA device, reserved test or network source accessed by this review.
This does not assert CUDA equivalence or admit scientific training. Root must run and inspect the bounded proof on the declared physical device.
Root must enforce a whole-invocation outer timeout and current process/device ownership; the validator has signal handling but no autonomous wall-clock deadline.
Bounded replay artifacts contain explicit non-scientific purpose/configuration and must never be promoted to final-cohort models.
